A job applicant submits job applications to companies. The job applicant must regularly report the companies to which they submitted job applications. 

For each job application, a company confirms receipt and rates the application. The company and the job applicant can negotiate a job interview. If the company wants the job applicant to work for them, the job applicant enters the probation phase. 

During the probation phase, the job applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the job applicant. After the probation phase, if the job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless the job applicant rated the company C or less. If the job applicant rated the company C or less, the process continues, but the job applicant no longer has to report job applications, and they continue to receive new job offers from the company.

maternity_leave.reformulated_text:
To support planning, taking, and extending a maternity leave, a process can be created with the following steps:

1. Fetch information about potential maternity leave models, including their duration in months and any split between parents.
2. Present the parent with the available models to select from.
3. Collect relevant information from the parent, such as their leave preferences and requirements.
4. Notify the Social Security and the Company of the parent's intention to take maternity leave in a timely manner.
5. Gather information from the Company regarding their maternity leave policies and any necessary procedures.
6. At the end of the maternity leave period, allow the parent to decide whether to extend their leave.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
To gather information about work accidents and almost work accidents, a process is created that involves several steps and actors. The process starts with the definition of a work accident, which is an accident that occurs in specific circumstances related to insured gainful employment. 

A work accident is considered to be an accident that occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment. This includes accidents that occur when working from home, on the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work, to lunch, or on the way home, including carpools. It also includes accidents that occur on the direct route from home, or from the workplace or training centre to a doctor and back, if this interrupts the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work or the route home. 

Additionally, a work accident is considered to be an accident that occurs when making use of advocacy groups or professional associations, such as the Chamber of Labour, trade union federation, guild, etc. For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, a work accident is considered to be an accident that occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education or the compulsory kindergarten year that forms the basis of the insurance. 

This includes accidents that occur when taking part in a school event or school-related event, on the direct route from the child's place of residence or permanent accommodation to kindergarten or a school visit or on the way home, and when performing a practical task prescribed as part of the curriculum and/or the study regulations. 

In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment, including working in the household of the owner, providing accommodation for guests, secondary occupations for selling agricultural products, building work for the establishment, and neighbourhood assistance for another establishment. 

Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents outside of professional activity, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident or donating blood, and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation. 

The employees must inform the employer immediately of any work accident, any incident that would almost have led to an accident, any serious and immediate risk to safety and health that they discover, and any defect discovered in protection systems. 

The employer must immediately report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been reported to the emergency services. 

Independent of this, every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed, or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days, in full or in part, must be reported to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days. 

As a self-employed person, accidents involving people you employ and those that involve you must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time. 

Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent directorate. Schools, educational facilities, and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate. 

In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported. 

The process involves the following actors: employees, employers, Labour Inspectorate, accident insurance providers, students, schoolchildren, schools, educational facilities, universities, and the competent directorate. The process starts with the occurrence of a work accident or an almost work accident, and it involves the reporting of the accident to the employer, the Labour Inspectorate, and the accident insurance provider. 

The process also involves the reporting of accidents by students and schoolchildren to the competent directorate, and by schools, educational facilities, and universities to the responsible accident insurance provider. The process is time-sensitive, and the reporting of accidents must be done within a specific timeframe to avoid any consequences. 

The process is also dependent on the type of insurance, and in the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported.
